text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 3 – enhanced wifi, improved motion detection, easy installation Great wireless camera/doorbell. Hardware/software this is ideal. We live on a busy street so we were getting lots of notifications. The software allowed us to adjust where the camera sensed motion, cutting down "false" notifications. Easy to use.
Easy to setup and install. Took maybe 15 minutes from opening the box to having it up and running.
Convenient set-up and access via phone (iOS and Android) app. Added skill to Echo, so when someone sets of camera or pushes doorbell, we get a notification via Alexa, and an image on the Echo show. You can adjust how often and what notifications you receive in the app.
Night vision is pretty good as well. Another nice feature is you can access a "live" view anytime, notification or not.
Audio works well, so if you are in the basement, garage, at work, shopping you can talk to whomever is at your door.
If you carry your phone everywhere or have a smart home speaker (Google, Echo or maybe Apple?) you won't need the additional chime, phone and speakers have a decently loud sound.
I would suggest getting a second battery if you have a busy street or lots of activity. The app notifies you in plenty of time the battery is low and needs to be recharged (only takes a couple hours to fully charge). But a second battery extends the life and less work (but to be fair, one screw using included driver, slide off plate, slide battery out, set to charge and reverse process to put battery back in. With two batteries, the whole thing takes about two minutes. With one, you simply have a non-functioning doorbell/camera for a few hours. No biggie, just FYI.
Also there is an an App called Neighbors free to join and use. It lets you share "videos and notifications of criminal or suspicious activity. So if someone in your neighborhood is broken into or home is vandalized they can share the video and/or share a notice of the incident. Lost dog, share. Delivery thieves, share. So both kinda cool and scary.
Now the BAD. To access the video you have to pay a monthly fee ( now if you access the video within the first 30 seconds or so, you are golden, but if you have your hands full, or can't access your phone, you can't see the video, or back it up. While the basic few is like $40 ish a year. Higher for the next tier up. That is forever. And no easy way to back up to a local storage device. All files are on Rings servers.
Now if you know that up front, and $40 is no biggie. Then 5 stars.
But for me that is an issue.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 3 – enhanced wifi, improved motion detection, easy installation

The ball head is easy to adjust and has an intuitive friction control lever which allows you to move the ball head just a little or a lot. I feel like I've got great control. I also really liked the turning action of the quick release knob, it feels a lot more secure than the usual lever that I'm used to.

Overall, this is a great addition to my humble set of landscape photography and video equipment. It's easy to use, took me about two minutes to figure out and attach, and gives me much better functionality than I had previously.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon PowerShot SX500 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 30x Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 3.0-Inch LCD (Black) (OLD MODEL) I recently took this camera, along with my PowerShot Elph 110, on a Caribbean cruise. Because I have the waterproof case for the 110, I used it whenever I was shooting in wet areas and also for underwater shots. I used the SX500 in dry locations. In some instances, I was able to take comparable shots with both cameras and the difference was really striking. Let me preface this by saying that I'm NOT a photographer. I'm just someone who likes to take a lot of pictures. I like them to come out well, but I know virtually nothing about photography beyond what I've learned through trial and error.

I found the low-light shots taken with the SX500 to be FAR superior than those taken with the Elph. Yes, it's difficult to capture a moving subject in low light. This isn't and expensive, professional camera. I'm very pleased with the results considering the price I paid.

The biggest selling feature was the zoom lens. I was absolutely AMAZED how clear shots taken from VERY far away came out. I took this camera to Opening Day, to see the Red Sox players get their World Series rings. We didn't have the best of seats, so I had to really max out the zoom lens. I was certain the photos would be blurry. It's difficult to hold a camera really still, extremely zoomed in, while standing in a crowd. The photos were OUTSTANDING. I mean really...outstanding!

I'm extremely pleased with this purchase. The camera is small and easy to carry with the strap around my neck. When I want something I can slip in my pocket, I opt for the Elph.

I would classify this as a bridge camera. It's NOT as easy to carry around as a pocket-sized digital, but it's also not as cumbersome to carry around as a more professional model. It's EASY to use...even for novices like me! And it takes great photos. I'm sure as I have more trial-and-error lessons under my belt, my shots will be even better.
text_fidelity_b: Canon PowerShot SX500 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 30x Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 3.0-Inch LCD (Black) (OLD MODEL)

Blink XT Home Security Camera System - 5 Camera Kit - 1st Gen I had an Arlo set-up, and while I really liked it, I was constantly changing batteries. (Busy street).
I saw these read some good reviews and liked the battery life.
Plus they take regular AA batteries. Easy to install. But the hangers are not very flexible, you are limited in how you are able to position the camera. For example, I have one camera up on the side of my carport, and I need for it to tilt down and to the left. With the provided hanger, that is not possible. I will make an adapter for this, but after th ease of positioning of the Arlos, I am disappointed.
Set-up was a breeze, after hanging them where I wanted them, I opened the mobile app, connected them to the supplied Bridge, and Wifi. Made adjustments to various app settings and done, reading instructions, hanging and set-up in under an hour. One of the nice aspects is the zones, (you can "block" areas from motion detection on individual cameras. so Doorways or street, sidewalks, etc to fit high traffic and pedestrian areas.
The presets are nice, but for some like me who have unusual areas to cover, some time and subtle adjustments will be needed.
The storage provided for free is adequate for me.
What I am not a fan of is the delay in recording, a couple seconds, but enough time for things/people to move out of camera view.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse At first I was skeptical about the idea of using my left hand for this. I was initially expecting it to be a replacement mouse for my right hand, but after more research I understood what they are trying to do. I must say that it's much easier to use than I expected, and operating it with my left hand works just fine.

I was also hesitant because of the price. However, this mouse is fantastic. Worth every penny. I'm using it with SketchUp, and it's vastly easier and faster than the normal built-in navigation tools. It's hard to articulate just how awesome this is. Once you get used to it, it's instinctive and effortless, and moving around the model is so easy! You will absolutely love it.

There was one tricky thing during the setup, however. I plugged it in, loaded the driver, and launched SketchUp. Then I found and opened the configuration window to customize it for SketchUp. The info I had found showed that configuration window with "SketchUp" at the top, and the SketchUp-specific options. But my configuration window didn't have anything specific to SketchUp. It said Windows Explorer at the top instead of SketchUp. I thought I was missing a driver. I messed around a log time, and looked through lots of online info.

At one point, I noticed it said Chrome instead of Windows Explorer. That's when I figured it out. The configuration window changes by itself, based on what application is active. I had SketchUp running in the background, but my most recent activity was with Windows Explorer and then Chrome. With the configuration window open, I clicked over into the SketchUp window, and suddenly the configuration window said SketchUp at the top, and the the SketchUp-specific settings appeared. I wish that had been in the instructions somewhere!!

At first I didn't bother programming the buttons, but later I tried it, and that's an awesome feature. For Sketchup, I programmed one button to be "remove guides", and the other is "paste in place". Hitting those buttons is much faster than finding those things in the menu each time. However, I discovered that I need to make sure I'm not moving through the model when I press the "paste in place" button, or the mouse locks up, and I need to restart SketchUp. But as long as I make sure I'm not moving when I press it, I never have that problem anymore.

Anyway, you will absolutely love this. After using it, I no longer had any doubt about it being worth the money. It's worth every penny. I would give it 6 stars if I could.
text_fidelity_b: 3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output The MyCharge is a handy if not tiny clamshell charging case for PowerBeat headphones, though it will work for others as well.

Pros:
The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.
text_fidelity_b: myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output

text_fidelity_a: Pioneer Electronics Audition Series XW_NAS3-K Docking Station for iPod (Black) I was the happy owner of the original Bose sounddock for seven years until it stopped working this November.  I thought that was a very good run.  To replace the Bose I chose the Pioneer NAS3 and waited a month for the price to drop to $220.  I like the clean design as I wasn't looking for a display nor was I looking for an alarm clock.  On first play I was not at all impressed with the muddy flat sound until I found that under the music menu on the ipod is a setting for 'speakers'.  Going into 'speakers' I can enhance the sound with the bass/treble on setting which is comparable to the ipod EQ acoustic setting.  You can really bump up the sound by turning on both but for me the sound becomes unnaturally bright and the bass distorts.  In other words the dock does respond to all ipod EQ settings.  Under 'speakers' I can also set the ipod display to always be on, always be off, or only come on when I press a key on the dock or on the remote.  Speaking of the remote, the range is strangely bad as you need to point it almost directly at the unit.  To make the NAS bluetooth capable then you'll need to buy the adaptor separately.  I don't know if it's only the Pioneer adaptor that will work but if that's the case, it's a pricey option at about $70. If this were an issue for me I would have rated the Pioneer three stars.  The sound quality here just doesn't earn it a five-star rating but I'll be keeping the unit.  If I had it to do it over again I would go with another Bose.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Electronics Audition Series XW_NAS3-K Docking Station for iPod (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel The lifetime warranty on this doorbell is the real deal. This is a very well-supported doorbell.

I was having issues with holiday season package thieves and a non-working wireless doorbell. Ring is the only video doorbell I could find that will work wirelessly. The first one had battery issues. Replaced no problem. The second one had sound issues. Replaced no problem. The third on works FLAWLESSLY. I absolutely love it.

The smart motion sensor works well. I see everyone who comes onto my porch, but not my neighbors' porches (three doors lined up on one big house). Two way sound is mostly good -> if it's really windy, it's hard to hear sometimes. The video is way better than I thought it would be. I can see well enough on my phone, but if I download and watch on my computer, it is very impressive.

I signed up for the cloud recording - it's the least expensive pay service of any of my security cameras, and it has been reliable over the few weeks I have been using it. The doorbell is also conspicuous enough to act as a deterrent. I've had a couple of alerts where people looked like they were going to come up the steps and then changed their minds. Both my postal carrier and my UPS driver said that a lot of their stops have these, and they really like them.

Bottom line: It took a couple of tries, but I am one hundred percent happy with this doorbell. If you have an issue, use the warranty. It's a real thing.

UPDATE: I have a CHIME now, as well, and it also works beautifully. The Ring Company gave it to me for free as a promotion, because I had bought two of their doorbells.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel

text_fidelity_a:
Audio-Technica ATH-M50xBT2 Wireless Over-Ear Headphones, Black I plan to start recording music of my own at home. So, I've been researching everything I'd need. A decent pair of monitor headphones are at the top of the "essential" list. I figured that if I were going to be spending money on some headphones, I'd like them to work casual use as well as mixing. So, after lots of digging, reading reviews, watching comparison videos, I have determined that the M50x would be the best for me, for the following reasons:

* Excellent sound quality
* Relatively flat response rate
* Comfortable with glasses
* Detachable cables (included with purchase)
* Reasonably affordable

I'm glad I put in all the legwork ahead of time. These arrived yesterday, and I've worn them for several hours, listening to music (mostly rock, metal and pop) and playing games (Diablo 3 and Skyrim.) The sound quality is outstanding. Admittedly, these are the first studio monitors I've listened to. I've owned decent "fun" headphones in the past (~$50 range) and these are by far superior to what I've experienced.

It took me a bit to settle on these, as some folks claimed that they were either bass heavy, harsh, or uncomfortable. Fortunately, I've found none of this to be true. I've had these on for up to 2 hours with no discomfort what-so-ever. When it comes to the sound, all I can say is "wow!" Everything is extremely clear, and I feel, balanced. The bass is definitely there, but it's not overpowering, and it certainly doesn't detract from other frequencies. The high end comes in really well, and not harsh at all to me. The layers in the music I've listened to so far are so much easier to distinguish.

In the past, I've been able to accurately distinguish various bitrate MP3s/audio files over laptop speakers (128 vs 256 vs lossless.) These headphones make it way easier.

Update - I've recently tried 2 other sets of headphones that my be somewhat comparable: Rockville Pro M50's and the Sony WHCH710N. The M50x's are by far better than both. The Rockville headphones are 1/3 the price and actually pretty close, if you take the price into comparison. The Audio Technicas are a fair amount clearer with nicer highs and lows. The Sony headphones were fairly disappointing, and I wouldn't recommend them, unless you needed wireless. I'm still very happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Audio-Technica ATH-M50xBT2 Wireless Over-Ear Headphones, Black

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions This GPS is a real upgrade for me, but I still love my old one which is TomTom One. Too bad it's no longer supported by TomTom or I probably would not have chosen the TomTom Via 1525 to try out for review. The very first thing I noticed about it was that the screen was twice as large as on my One - a very coveted perk to me. I choose to still use separate GPS devices instead of my phone since my phone uses up data and the GPS doesn't, saving me $$.

I have only used the Via 1525 a couple of times and it worked perfectly. I had to make a new account to TomTom to update it and overall it took about an hour and a half. I had a couple of problems with the update and had to restart but it finally worked. It comes with a USB for charging from a computer and another to use in the auxiliary power port in the car, and a mounting disk to adhere to a good spot in the car. It's not as intuitive as I would like, but it's not hard to figure out and it took us straight to our destination both times. I purposely passed some streets it was telling to me turn on to just to see how fast it would recalculate a route and it recalculated quickly. It has a lot of options that are indicated on the product page, most of which I will probably not use.

It's too early yet to give it 5 stars, but definitely 4 for now. It's a GPS, it found satellites quickly, got me a route planned out and was easy to follow. What more do I want from it? I like it a lot. It's supposed to have lifetime traffic and lifetime maps.......or until TomTom stops supporting it too.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

House of Marley Uprise: Wireless Earphones with Microphone, Bluetooth Connectivity, 8 Hours of Playtime, and Sustainable Materials (Teal) I have a lot of styles of headphones, and I now know what this type is perfect for: exercising. Maybe you and everyone else already knew this. But if I'm running (or elliptical-ing), regular ear buds may fall out, and bigger headphones can fall off or at least get uncomfortable sweaty. Obviously, you don't want a cord connected to your phone for exercising, so these hit the sweet spot in all those ways.

They are very comfortable as well. The ear pieces that come connected are a perfect fit for my ears, and already offer real sound-proofing from the outside world (warning: you may appear to be an annoying millennial if you walk around isolated from the world with these all the time). They are comfortable, and I love the easy way that the ear-hanger pieces are removable. I also like that you can tighten up the connecting strap. There must be a cable in there, so I hope it doesn't wear out this way, but it seems to be pretty durable, so I guess it will be okay.

Actually, these are great. The charging area is barely large enough for the micro-USB port, but the battery lasts for quite a few hours. Not as long as some headphones, but the low weight is key here.

Also good for: watching movies or listening to music on planes if you have your own device. No cord to slow you down when a seat-mate wants to get past you, and they're comfortable enough to fall asleep in, unlike over-the-head headphones.

Oh, I saw a review that said the bass was poor. I do not agree. Music sounds great in these. They can operate on low power because they are so far up in your ear. Be careful to keep them at a reasonable level.

I would recommend these to friends.

Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121) I read through Comcast supported model list and ordered this from another website, so I didn't have to pay their modem rental fee. I ordered Comcast using the online application process (borrowing a wireless connection from a neighbor), and was forced to order their starter package. Supposedly there is a way to refuse this if you call, but I didn't do this. I had a coax cable with me so as soon as I made my order I connected the modem to the coax input in the apartment, and my wireless router to the modem. I did not use a splitter. With my computer I tried to connect to the web which brought me to the comcast activation screen. I had no issues activating based on the info I had from the box and my comcast account number. This part was easy. It's a good thing I had my own cable since the starter package took two weeks to arrive.

My impression of this modem is that there is nothing special to this modem.You can access the modem through its IP address, which gives you several tabs: Status, Signal, Addresses Configuration, Logs, Open Source. No password is needed. You can remotely reboot it, and check to see if there is a signal. Other than that one feature I wished it had is having the ability to export logs. When the modem reboots, the logs get reset.

I have used a DOCSIS 2.0 modem at another location and I think the level of service makes a bigger difference than the DOCSIS version of the modem in use. You might see a difference if you pay for the top end ISP package, but I didn't get that. My plan is Performance which is supposed to be 50 Mbps, but my actual speed is 29 up 6 down.

I have read of some cases of the modem randomly rebooting. I don't have this issue. But I did open my modem and attached an aluminum heat sink as a precaution. I have managed to fit 100x25x10mm heatsink by cutting off a section. From what I read random reboots might be ISP related, but I'm not sure.

*****

As a side note, Comcast is terrible. At one point my service suddenly stopped. One tech service person I talked to hung up on me after half an hour of troubleshooting when see seemingly ran out of ideas to try. The next time I called I demanded a technician, which was scheduled to show up in 10 days at the earliest. I had a service outage for almost a month. The issue was a loose cable in their box. Also at one point my Netflix streaming was heavily throttled until Netlix payed off Comcast.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121)

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) [[VIDEOID:c23012732deceb9d78b96d41ac89bfcb]] [[VIDEOID:56e6589f81a80deb1709b51fc87a42ef]] [[VIDEOID:bdf9b77251e219b84bed6372225dbf2a]] [[VIDEOID:838bfc2c03ad2a6d884b05f4a37eddbe]] [[VIDEOID:f7f3bb80516774e2cc828f076249211a]] [[VIDEOID:d48cd1a96b9a119e675001d320845a53]] [[VIDEOID:9363c8a20797fe64545aeb51179ca502]] [[VIDEOID:3371609d21e77efbab0cfd0f6265a782]] This is a terrific little action camera that has remarkable clear video, good audio and is extremely easy to use. I understand there were some problems with audio in the earlier versions, but it seems to be all fixed now because the sound quality was excellent when tested both indoors and outside.

I won't bore you with going over all of the specs which you can read in the product description, but I'll tell you how easy it is to use. Mine arrived partially charged, so I used my fingernail to open the back port and inset the included 8gb micro SD card, then charged it fully within an hour. On a full battery it can operate for about 107 minutes and when depleted it takes between 1.5 to 2 hrs to fully charge.

I downloaded the app to my iPad for free from the app store, then did some testing. It connected easily to my WiFi and the interface understandable and easy to use giving you the choice to shoot still photos or videos in several different resolutions. You can also import the photos or videos taken with the camera to your cell phone, your iPad, or share them using the WiFi connection to import them.

This little camera takes gorgeous high def photos, and the audio inside is crystal clear. When I was offered the opportunity by the manufacturer to test the Cube+ I went ahead and purchased a [[ASIN:B00NXK3JTI Polaroid Helmet Mount for the Polaroid CUBE, CUBE+ HD Action Lifestyle Camera]] so I would be able to properly test it in action in order to determine video and sound quality outside in the elements.

I attached the helmet mount to my 9 y/o granddaughter's helmet, placed the Cube+ in it, started it through the app on my iPad and sent her out on her scooter to see how the video and audio quality was. I've attached a short part of the video here so you can assess it for yourself, but I'm quite pleased with the quality of both the picture and the sound, and I didn't experience any lag time in regards to the app.

It does record video in MP4 format, so if you have trouble hearing the audio on your computer you should download QuickTime Player or VLC Player. Both downloads are free and should allow you to view the files and hear the audio. VLC also has a free converter available in case you prefer to use Windows Media Player or Windows Movie Maker. I use a free app called Trim & Cut on my iPad which shortens, condenses, and converts my videos to the format I prefer, and that's what I used for the video I've attached here.

This is a reasonably priced tough little action camera that's easy to use and produces great quality video. It's weather resistant and splashproof so it can handle the outdoors already, but I plan to buy the waterproof case for it so we can have fun swimming with it on this summer. I don't own a GoPro, so I have nothing to compare this to, but from a user's stand point I can definitely tell you that this is user friendly, easy to operate and does a remarkably good job! Enjoy!

This camera was provided at no cost by the manufacturer for evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

Speed wise any SSD is good. I also own a Crucial M500 that I installed in my Linux laptop with SATA I, which is reported to be much slower but in practice proved to be x10 faster than the original laptop hard drive. For all of my other computers what makes the Samsung nice is the software. With Samsung Magician Software I can adjust over provisioning and see if any updates are needed. It also gives you a lists (profiles) of some items that you might need to adjust in your OS to make the SSD run optimally. It will also show you the health status, how many writes have been made and it can do a speed benchmark (though this can be done by other free software too). Samsung also provides migration software, but I never used that since I prefer to install from scratch.

Of course the brand reliability is probably the most important. I wouldn't touch OCZ drives for example, even if they were free.

I saw that this one was cheap and had mostly positive reviews, so I thought I'd take a chance on it. With free super saver shipping, it arrived in about a week and a half and it was exactly as I expected it would be from reading the reviews. It is true what several of the reviews have mentioned, the screws that come with it truly do not hold the end cap in the case (which means that the hard drive can slip in and out). It was a fairly simple fix; I just had to find some other screws that actually held it together. Another thing that's been mentioned is that there is no way to turn the enclosure off, i.e. if the drive is plugged into the computer it will be on regardless of if the computer is on or not (at least in my experience).

Conclusion: A good product if you need/want a hard drive enclosure and don't want to spend a lot. Having to find different screws and not being able to turn the drive off without unplugging it from the computer keep it from being five stars.

That's my two cents.

In the end I decided I wanted mainly a fitness tracker that has some smartwatch features, and that I wouldn't use most of the features on an actual smartwatch.

PROS

The app is awesome! My husband is a software developer so I learn a lot about what makes good apps good and what makes bad apps bad. This app is free and user friendly. It has mostly accurate measurements and you can easily track your progress and areas of improvement. It also has a feature that allows whoever you send the link to to track your location, in case you are concerned about getting kidnapped on your run. Very good stuff.

The steps I get seem to be pretty consistent as well as the distance traveled. The heartrate tracker seems to be mostly accurate (checked with manual pulse check).

The battery life is pretty good. Obviously I would use more battery if I am using the fitness modes. Depending on your activity level and use of the fitness modes, the battery could last you all week plus some. The battery charges to full in about 30 minutes.

I like the rectangular watch face and the light green band. I also like that you can change the bands. Apparently for some of the expensive FitBit models the band is not changeable so some people just buy a whole new watch. Like whaaat?

CONS
I like being able to see the texts I get on the watch, but I don't really care for receiving phone calls (I get so many spam calls that I don't even answer my phone lol). I don't think there is a way to say 'no' to having phone calls, so I get frequent notifications to enable phone call permissions. It's not too much of a problem but it's kind of annoying sometimes.

I think the sleep tracker is interesting, but I don't think it is accurate. I think that as long as you are "resting" during the hours that you put as your sleeping hours under Settings, that it considers this as sleep. Sometimes I can't sleep but the device considers this as light sleep. I think this would be an interesting addition, that perhaps it could be integrated: I am a night shift worker and I switch between day/night sleep, so I have to manually enter my bedtimes in the app's User Settings to sleep. I think that if there was an activity button, like when you choose walk/run/cardio on the watch itself, for sleep, it would be easier for me personally. I am not sure if that could be done with a software update or if this is a hardware type thing.

FINAL THOUGHTS

I wear this watch almost 24/7 and I think it has helped me consider and evaluate my activity levels as well as track my improvement. I think that if Garmin made a watch that had the aesthetics and watch interface comparable to the Apple watch but kept the good fitness aspect, I would definitely purchase as an upgrade.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black

Have a hub of some sort that can be put anywhere nearish to the cameras, and then that can connect wirelessly to an app, computer, or monitor on the same network, not just for setup, but in general.

We would have had to go from the garage area to the inside part of the house, somewhere over 70 feet? To get to the nearest tv or monitor.

I'll try again for my small business if we ever change locations, but having to attach to a monitor is a pain. It should be able to work directly from the hub/DVR to an app.

Fujifilm FinePix Z90 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 5x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch Touch-Screen LCD (Red) This camera is what I call a "subcompact" - the smallest point and shoot cameras that have vertically mounted lenses which allow protection, compactness, and quicker start up times. Normally, you'd expect a small trade off for these features, so I wouldn't compare this directly with a camera endowed by a telescoping lens.

Sony invented the subcompact with the T1 a few years back (at least in my world), and I was able to compare the FinePix Z90 with the one-generation-older 12 MP Sony T90. I'll go the pro/con route...

PROS of the Z90:

-Price is something like half of the latest subcompact Sony.
-Operational costs are cheaper: USB cable is non-proprietary (in case you want a second one or need to replace it) and SD card is cheaper and more universal than Sony's Memory Stick.
-Separate physical buttons to record movies and to take pictures. This is genius to me, because I hate to miss a great video opportunity while fumbling through the menus.
-Does not come with a memory card, BUT cameras that do usually come with one so small that it is worthless. Internal memory is better, because it allows you to copy from one camera card to another, which can be useful.
-Can set it up to take two photos at once, with and without the flash. As an amateur, I often do this manually anyway, but this way you get closer photos (chronologically)to compare in a dynamic scenario, and the subject needs only to pose once.
-The panorama mode works better than in other cameras I've used. They use internal weights alla smart phones (I'm guessing) to help you line up the next picture. Allows you to "pan" a panorama shot in play mode.
-There is a time zone mode that allows you to temporarily change the time (for timestamps).
-The display changes from horizontal to vertical as you move the camera respectively.
-"Touch and track" mode follows a subject.
-Side by side picture compare.
-Search by face, couple, group, favorites, scene, or date, and view a small picture next to thumbnails.
-Charger is smaller with the plug offset to allow it to use only one receptacle on a power strip (as long as it is at the end of said strip).

CONS of the Z90:

-Picture quality was not as good as the Sony 80% of the time (tested in various modes and lighting conditions). That said, a tripod really helps with low light and no flash, where both cameras struggle without it.
-By numbers, it is not much larger than the Sony, but it feels significantly larger.
-Sometimes the "buttons" in the corners of the touch screen need to be pressed more than once.
-Tripod mount has plastic threads, instead of a machined metal insert.
-Cannot take shots as rapidly as on the Sony
-Does not tell you what zoom level you are at. 5x zoom does not appear to make a great difference over 4x.
-"play" and "camera" buttons could be one button used as a toggle.
-Battery can be put in backward, as the slot is not keyed (although the battery is). No big deal, but shows something wasn't thought out thoroughly.

Bottom Line:

The Fuji is trying to deliver everything the market leader has to offer for a much more manageable price tag. It gets an A for effort, delivering a lot of great menu options, and may actually win in that respect, but the picture quality is not as good. If they could pour a little more money into the actual optics and the touch screen and still keep the price reasonable, they might win the battle in the future. For now, it's purely a personal budget vs. quality decision.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix Z90 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 5x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch Touch-Screen LCD (Red)

Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White This is an extremely comfortable to wear set of lightweight over-ear headphones.

There's often a lot of noise in my house. A television on somewhere, dishes being done, and a nine year old that never stops talking. I like to use headphones as an escape. When headphones claim they are noise isolating I hold them to it. These headphones did not disappoint me. The nicely cushioned soft pleather covered ear cups adjust for angle to offer a secure fit that provides excellent insulation against ambient noise and are very comfortable to wear, even for extended periods of time.

I found that they could deliver the snap of live instruments, or the impression that I was at a club with the singer on the stage in front of me. When the music had stopped, there was still silence. I noticed that I enjoyed wearing them because of the peace and quiet, I didn't want to take them off actually. These headphones isolate out noise so well they made me consider wearing them when the kid's home just to be able to hear myself think.

The sound quality is crisp, great clarity not overpowering and provide a personal ambience. They offer a great balance and at no point was I confused when watching movies. They were even picking up the weighty and seismic bass from Jurassic Park that would imply a dinosaur was right behind me. The adjustable aluminum headphone band has a slight amount of padding beneath the pleather covered top part, but I wish it had just a little bit more to provide a bit more cushioning. Finally, the headphones are able to smoothly swivel flat for storage or packing although the cable is too long for me to want to use these for trips.

Overall I am incredibly happy with their quality, especially for the price. They're very comfortable, provide excellent noise isolation, and deliver very clean response with deep bass. I plan to enjoy using them and am pleased to recommend them on Amazon.

Retail sample provided at no cost by Edifier for my testing, evaluation, and review.

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RCRPS06GR 6 Device Universal Remote What occurred to me after wasting half an hour with this thing is that what is needed is an iPhone app to control your television and stereo, not a single freaking light bulb and a long, long list of codes printed in mouse type.

See photo. The remote looks good, shiny Darth Vader black. There are three manuals, one of which is about an ounce and a half. One is a long list of codes and the third unfolds to about 10x17 so that between the three differently-sized printed manuals you have a lap full of clutter which is difficult to manage while you're trying to press buttons in some order.

I couldn't get it to do much of anything, and by the time I realized that half an hour had gone by and I was getting hot under the collar, I thought: FAIL. Why waste any more of my time? Ah, but by THAT time I was and am good and frustrated at this RCA product. RCA. Who knew they were still in business? Who the heck would buy an RCA product? I'm sure they made great gramophones back in the day, but Sony came by and ate their lunch and even that was forty years ago.

If you were an RCA exec, wouldn't you want to make certain that anything your company made was functional? I've got a couple college degrees. I can tie my own shoes. I can do all kinds of things, but I couldn't figure out how to program this little (EXPLETIVE DELETED) thing. Which frustrates me.

The first thing I noticed (after I cut the I-dare-you-to-open-me hard plastic packaging) was that it hurt to open the battery compartment. There's some idiotic L-shaped trigger you have to depress, meaning that you're digging it under your fingernails, which I think most people would find painful. Just a dumb design move. No other word for it. Dumb.

The remote looks good and has some interesting ribs underneath it. The buttons are not what you might expect, the volume and channel buttons are flabby feeling and weak, not definite-feeling. The center "OK" button is kind of clicky, like cellophane. There's a whole array of buttons, but it's not worth my time to try and program each one. And I grew to dislike the hard plastic feeling of the remote. There are other plastic materials that feel better to the hand. LOOK AT SONY PRODUCTS, RCA, LOOK AT SONY PRODUCTS FOR A FREE CLUE.

I'm annoyed and frustrated. This seemed like such a neat idea. But sitting on my couch juggling three differently-sized manuals AND this remote and wondering why none of these instructions were doing anything was really frustrating, just not how I want to spend my free time. I'll happily continue to exist with my TV remote, my surround-sound remote, my AppleTV remote and the AT&T cable box remote, you know? BECAUSE THEY WORK and they work without frustrating me.

Here's my idea: RCA hires an app developer and somehow figures out how to have your devices tell the app what their codes area. Something like that. Because the notion of combing through a manual full of codes in tiny type is worse than doing your income taxes.

THE WORLD HAS MOVED ON, RCA and you are apparently living in the 1970s with burgundy leisure suits and avocado-colored kitchen appliances.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS REMOTE, IT WILL ONLY FRUSTRATE YOU and dig in the skin under your nails. Ouch. Did this thing really have to be so frustrating? Do you imagine this is the kind of experience consumers are after? Not just one more freaking remote control, but one that promises convenience and delivers frustration? Not a good product. Stay away from it.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RCRPS06GR 6 Device Universal Remote

text_fidelity_a:
BUGANI Bluetooth Speakers, M83 Speaker IPX6 Waterproof Portable LargeWireless Speaker,Bluetooth 5.2, Wireless Two Pairing,24H Playtime,Suitable for Family Gatherings and Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker I ordered this for the higher wattage and on my primary phone, it does get quite loud; but on my Dex device, it's maxed out is equivalent to about 50% volume on a 10W speaker.
I used a dB meter that was about 6ft away with the speaker pointed towards the meter. At max volume on my main phone (fold3) and at 150% volume, I was getting a consistent mid-90s dB for melody and lyrics, with peaks up to 109dB. On my other device (Note 10+), also at 150%, it was pulling about 70 dB on TV dialogue. I did try testing it with a volume booster, and even with only 110% (on top of the 150%) it was beginning to distort.
I played the TV audio for about 16hrs at moderate and 8hrs on low, and it was reading as still having 70% battery. But after only a few hours of moderate-high volume music, that 70% was gone and it died.
The sound quality is quite good with a warm tone. The highs are clear and the bass is better than I expected for there not to be a dedicated bass cone.
Despite appearances, I think the best use for this will be background music - not too loud will keep it playing all day & night and it will provide a much cleaner and richer sound than a small speaker at similar volume.
text_fidelity_b: BUGANI Bluetooth Speakers, M83 Speaker IPX6 Waterproof Portable LargeWireless Speaker,Bluetooth 5.2, Wireless Two Pairing,24H Playtime,Suitable for Family Gatherings and Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker

Get a 32GB chip, put CHDK on it and you can do awesome stuff with this camera. I bought two for my family's trip to Alaska, and we snapped thousands of photos. Very good quality, fair low light performance, controls are easy enough. We spent a fair bit of time learning the controls so we'd be fluent with them.

Here's a neat trick: You can use these cameras as low power microscopes. Put the Macro setting on, take a photo as near ask the thing will focus, which is pretty close, then hit 'Play' and use the zoom lever on the shutter release to zoom in and get a microscope view of what you took the photo of.

Also, with CHDK on the SD card, you have a built in intervelometer for taking time lapse sequences.

Another fun thing to do is to take night time photos of the sky using the long exposure setting. With the 10 second setting and the ISO turned up you can capture images of stars or northern lights in the night sky. Fantastic for a $60 camera.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White) This tablet has entirely streamlined my educational, professional, and personal productivity. I will preface this by saying I chose this tablet (as my very first tablet of any kind) after 5 WEEKS of research and hours and hours of reading the manual, watching video of reviews, unboxing, customization, how-to's, tips and tricks, and specific software guides. I had the nexus 10 in my amazon shopping cart when I first came across this tablet. I will nowhere in this review compare this to an apple device- I have never and will never own one- personal preference, I wholeheartedly believe iOS is sufficient or ideal for a lot of people's use, just not ever going to be for mine. As background, I am in an international DVM program whose laptop just crashed and all 600+gigs of my life were backed up but now only floating in cyberspace so my requirements were a little heady for a tablet-

a) deal with extensive editing and review of PDFs, PPTs, DOCs, XLXS, etc 14-17hrs a day (terms range from 21-24 credits, 4-5hrs of lecture straight, 3-4 hrs of lab with no access to outlet in many labs). Also when I say edit I don't just mean take notes on I also mean incorporate text, figures, etc from textbooks, websites, and other documents.

b) Be a textbook reader and rarely a e-book reader (novels for fun!) Need to access my extensive kindle library, plus some google books and a few Elsevier/pageburst textbooks. Also this needs to be something I am comfortable and accepting of to literally study off of, enough to give up my previous preferring to only study off of paper/actual printed out notes

c) Allow for flawless email, web chat, skype video and text, some web browsing, and file transfer... all on an absolutely horrible school wireless and LAN setup, unpredictable power availability, etc.

d) Streaming and downloading of podcasts, video, MRI, CT, radiographs, and ECG's

e) Be portable to the clinic and the farms for patient-side transcription, recording, etc

f) Get me through the 5-6hr flight and all the airport time!

g) Occasionally watch videos/listen to things for fun

h) Most importantly, due to a dominant hand injury, multiple surgeries, and continued required hand therapy/rehab, I am currently able to write again but not to type with that hand. I therefore wanted a tablet that was stylus intensive- not just for notes, but for navigation, etc. THIS is what made me give up that wonderful squeaky clean android OS of the nexus 10! (I still thing that is probably the best thing for people that want an android tablet but don't NEED a stylus)
So my tablet arrived flawless and flawlessly. The display is beautiful, if anything the screen is too bright- I'm aware my eyes are light sensitive so this won't match with the majority of people but if I do turn my brightness on at all I don't believe I've ever gone above 15%, though I'm sure there will be some case videos poorly and darkly shot that I may need to in the future.

i) at least temporarily, replace my laptop and download and have as much of my backed up laptop files as possible

The tablet was quickly populated with the apps from my HTC phone and google account. The account set up for everything was quick and easy. The initial 2 updates were completed with no adverse signs. Navigation was great, no lag, and I quickly cleared out the stock widgets, set up my panes, and then went into settings.... I activated Developer options and did some customization and disabling there, but most of the disabling I did in app manager, device, and controls. There are very helpful guides out there if you're not sure which apps are safe to disable as well as a "Guide: Longer Battery Life- How You're Being Robbed on XDA that takes you step by step in maximizing your tablet. It was not created at the time when I cleaned up mine but it would've helped greatly!

Here is the gist. The tablet comes crammed full of software and capabilities that I don't need or want. The My Magazine app, a lot of the touchwiz stuff, the eye movement sensors(smart screen), the hand gesture stuff, reading mode, voice control, motions/palm motions, all of that is just a constant battery drain and I will never use them. They were disabled and the vibration feedback for everything was also turned off.

Battery Report: This tablet was shipped within the US twice, and was brought internationally on a plan 4 days later. It was accidently left on the ENTIRE time for about 8 days with six apps up on standby. It arrived with 18% battery left. I use it for 15-17hours a day and end up having to charge it 2-3hrs per about ever 24hr period to get it back to 100. I can use it while it is charging and it will still positively charge during use.

USE FOR A STUDENT: It has replaced textbooks, laptop, printer, scanner, and painstakenly editing and customizing notes and making documents for me. Disclaimer: as someone who used to be able to type 130+ words per minute, I'll make perfectly clear, if you prefer to type and plan on typing a LOT tablet touchscreen keyboards SUCK. This is a fact of life. You can get used to them, you can get proficient at them, but you'll still probably hate it and you're going to need a physical keyboard case/add on if you do a lot of typing of documents or emails. Now, this tablet is made for a stylus. This is not just a peculiarly edged simple piece of plastic that you can buy for just about any touchscreen device and kind of use as a writing device. This is the s-pen, a WACOM and this device and stylus is designed to maximize the experience so you are writing or drawing digitally with an experience just like on paper. Examples- the harder you press the more solid and thicker your pencil/pen/brush/highlighter/calligraphy/etc line. The button on the stylus brings up air command which can be super helpful and it also allows quick screen shots. The stylus allows for fine website navigation that allows you to open drop down windows etc as mouse would. It also offers things a real pen/pencil cant- selective erasing, and selection for drag/drop/copy/paste of ANYTHING to ANYWHERE. You're typing notes and see a great figure and text on a website, you can freehand or rectangular circle what you want and put it into your document. Then you can resize/edit. It's great. I've been using the Snote app for everything thus far, I have made short futile attempts with Lecture Notes and Evernote but I couldn't really get anywhere. I'm not going to give up on then, I just need to research them more to see if I can eventually get them to do what I want and then I can compare them to Snote.

USE FOR A PROFESSIONAL: So far, this has been wonderful. I can seamlessly take notes, look up references, voice record my exam findings, and awkwardly as only a tablet is, take video and pictures of patient's during an exam for later review. (Extremely helpful during lameness and neuro exams for the file). Collaborative documents through Polaris office and google drive is exceptional- as fast as a laptop and more portable, and better screen size than a smartphone. It runs better than the school computers for running presentations off of onto projectors. I can also have students I tutor digitally sign- literally our weekly sheets and submit them via email with one step- completely negating the awesome printer and scanner I brought down here.

USE FOR A CONSUMER: I find this tablet beautiful for watching movies and videos and the sound is great. In a classroom of 50 people chatting between classes I have no problem hearing the speakers among the hub but there are completely valid reports that even cranked the sound might get lost a little if you're in a very loud close crowd. Sound improves with earbuds but the initial audio set up app (basically a hearing test and then a customized audio scheme for you) was startling when it compared the stock/base line settings to what it came up with for ME.

USE FOR AN ARTIST: I'm still learning and adapting, I'll never turn to this instead of actual physical art supplies and paper but it is fun and I can really see myself doing more digital than before. It has been especially nice for graphic design, photoshopping, etc.

USE AS A LEFTY: no issues except see below for one thing that affects both right and left handers...

ISSUES: 1) One day after about a week of ownership, my battery was in the upper 80's, I was taking some notes and about 2hrs later I looked at the status bar and it was 29%. I went into Battery in Settings, and the s-pen interface was responsible for 80% of the battery use. I shut down and then restarted and it's never happened again. Similarly the Android OS did the same thing at a later instance but again it was a one time thing and in both cases the battery recharged speedily after and stayed charged.
2) Snote- I have had weird episodes where an import fails, or it force closes itself repeatedly when I try to rename or change the cover of one particular document. After this erratic behavior occurred twice in three days and completely clearing and restarting Snote from scratch (everything backed up and replaced on my Samsung account) to no avail, I did a factory reset. The last ¾ of my ownership have seen no such problems any more. I will warn you that if you wipe out S note and you start from scratch in it and re-transfer all your SNote files back in, if you have a lot of really big files, it can take a really long time to re-populate.
3) The menu/return and physical home button- occasionally based on the desk I'm at, if my arm isn't supported and my wrist is resting fully on the edge of the tablet, these buttons will get pressed while I'm writing. Its purely an annoyance and doesn't affect the writing or do anything but I definitely have to reposition if I find I'm getting lazy on holding my wrist up at these desks.

Wrap up: I only use in landscape, it's just like writing on a portrait piece of paper except you can also zoom. I got used to writing on the tablet and the tiny stylus very quickly but there are compatible Samsung styli of various widths and sizes out there as well. I thought about waiting for the new 12.2 whose screen is literally a full piece of paper landscape, but I realized this is perfect for me and more portable than the 12.2 will be (this thing can just squeeze into one of the pockets on one of my lab coats. I was planning on having to use the Nova launcher to avoid any lag but truly, this tablet was a speed demon already and I eventually got Nova solely for the customization ability and cleaner interface. It allows me to avoid more things I don't use and I didn't lose ANY of the software I do.

Bottom line, RESEARCH! PREPARE! And there will STILL BE A LEARNING CURVE! But it will be based on discovering unexpected cool features instead of on frustration). If you won't heavily use the stylus, don't spend the money on this tablet. If you're just curious if you could "get into a stylus" try one out first but prepare first so you can use it to the full advantage while you're there. Also, I came from NO tablet and no Samsung/Note experience and there are changes between the previous model and this. You don't actually lose much but things are moved around and different. Don't be scared to optimize it, I'm not talking rooting, though adventurous forays into that terrain have finally arrived as well. In conclusion I love it, it has made things so much more efficient for me, I get a lot DONE with it and it's basically all I have to carry around. I purchased the 32gig tablet plus a 64gig Sandisk XC which installed and worked like a charm. There are annoyances that come up but any issue I have had I have been able to fix. I have everything safely backed up on Carbonite and there's a million ways to sync all of your accounts if you chose (note some of this may be unnecessary or frequency can be dialed back too)

It performs and looks beautiful and I am still learning.

EDIT: FLASH PLAYER: This tablet absolutely supports flash. Youtube and embedded flash worked right out of the box, however, to watch my amazon video's etc, I just downloaded the following file- I cannot post the actual link but it's a drop box file. Install this and make sure flash is enabled in your browser settings/plugins and it will work in the stock browser, Dolphin, and Mozilla. Some people also recommend having your browser set to View Desktop site.

Edit 12/15/2014: Please see my comment under product question- "Can you use amazon prime video on the galaxy 10.1 2014 ed? asked by Judith C. Love on November 14, 2013" for instructions and the direct link for flash file

Edit 02/2017: My tablet got slammed by careless sleep-deprived brain addled 4th year vet students and the screen got shattered in the upper right corner. Still useable, not any real issues but concern about the little chips and cracks gradually loosening and only being held together by the screen protector I was itching to replace due to scratches but now couldnt, left me with the desire to replace as I was 4 months out of my extended warranty. Call it coincidence but literally as I powered up the replacement, this original tablet FAILED. The screen doesn't illuminate. At certain angle/light you can see it's on but there is no way for me to see well enough to unlock the screen and at least access over 3 years of my life on the original tablet. I am 99% convinced this is secondary to the trauma/screen break, and I had nearly everything backed up via Carbonite on the original except for the past few months of random downloads. Still, I am grieved and wanted a moment of silence.

Yes we had great times together but I am truly sad and a bit devastated because the replacement came with OS updates that I had been actively refusing to install for the past year. Thus, my new tablet in short, I can't stand. It's the same make and model except offers 4G which I don't use but it is unbearably slow (cant load my pdf vet school notes worth a damn- it's faster for me to find a computer, login to carbonite back up, download the enormous file and open it on the computer than to scroll through the pdf on the tablet one page per 10 seconds loading. It's truly unbearable. All the updates and changes are awful and its so slow despite me instantly ditching touchwhiz and using Nova Launcher.

Moment of silence for my beloved original, maybe one day science will advance enough for me to communicate with you without a working screen so that I can have you back. Laughingly, the one OS update I did do that slowed you down, turns out, compared to the ones that followed, you were still almost the speed of light comparatively.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White)

text_fidelity_a:
Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter Shooting video outdoors with a DSLR requires, obviously, proper exposure. When shooting at 24 (23.978) frames per second, the normal shutter speed should be 1/50th of a second (1/60 at 29.97 fps). If the camera is set at the lowest ISO rating of 100, in bright daylight the f/stop would be around f/22. If you want to operate at wider aperture to achieve shallow depth of field, you need to cut the light.

This variable density filter allows such an adjustment. The problem is that it cuts the light by rotating two polarizing filters against each other. Polarizers can be tricky and, by design, modify the quality of light. Thus it may act unexpectedly.

One downside is that the front of the filter is not threaded and my 77mm model is a larger diameter than the 70-200mm Nikon zoom it fits on. So now the bayonet lens hood won't fit. Now I'm outdoors with a filter on the lens and no hood to block flare. There aren't any hoods that naturally fit the filter so you need to tape a hood to the outer ring or use a matte box.
text_fidelity_b: Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S35 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - LJDS35-64GABNL (Assorted colors) The Lexar jump drive was the speediest drive I have, but it does feel a little more cheaply made than some. Some specifics:

I used a Macbook Pro, mid 2012
I copied over a folder with 3000 items in it, a mix of file types including video, photos, presentations, docs, PDFs, Final Draft, spreadsheets
This Lexar copied the files over in just under 5 minutes
An older Lexar USB 3.0 took exactly 8 minutes
A Transcend 3.0 took about 8.5 minutes
A Sandisk 2.0 took much longer. In the same time this Lexar took to fully copy the folder, the 2.0 Sandisk was less than a third of the way through

I did a bit more copying of fewer files and the results were consistent--this one was faster on a regular basis

Formatting for my Mac was fast and simple.

It comes with a 2-inch lanyard to attach to a key chain or whatever.

My single concern is build quality. It is plastic, like most of my flash drives, but it feels less sturdy, a bit more cheaply made. And it seems particularly thin at the outlet end (where the USB prong exits). If it breaks I'll update.

So far then, the speed is a definite plus. It's the fastest of my 3.0 flash drives. And certainly anyone with a 2.0 will want to upgrade--the difference, assuming you can take advantage of it, is hugely significant. Just that build quality to be worried about, but so far so good
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S35 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - LJDS35-64GABNL (Assorted colors)

text_fidelity_a: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Earbuds Headphones, Earphones with Microphone and Nylon Cable (Turquoise Blue). I have always been a big skullcandy fan (I know, I probably just lost most people reading this review, but hear me out). I am a hipster when it comes to skullcandy, I was skullcandy back in 07-08 when they were actually of quality. No different than the first set of beats that were good, and everything recent is subpar. Now, I continued purchasing skullcandy because I was never good to my earbuds. The average lifespan of my earbuds was about 2 months, so the cheap quality was fine. But when I started med school and had to study all the time, I found my earbuds finally lasted over a year, but the quality was bugging me. They wouldn't cancel out the annoying undergrads who used the library for socialization rather than studying. I decided to finally to invest in pair of higher quality earbuds. I was willing to spend beats price if I was going to get quality. Little did I know there existed a pair of earbuds roughly equal in price to my skullcandy, but outclasses them when it comes to quality. All of my friends who have tried these earbuds have had to switch. They have a great sound, noise cancel, and have a mic if you're into that. The one negative (hence the minus 1 star) is that the jack has this "nub" that when pressed in my pocket pauses my music. This is very annoying for walking to class or the bus. But when I'm sitting and studying, I would choose no other.
text_fidelity_b: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Earbuds Headphones, Earphones with Microphone and Nylon Cable (Turquoise Blue).

text_fidelity_a:
Philips SHQ3200BK/28 ActionFit Sports Earhook Headphones While they are ok for the price in terms of sound quality, fit, and durability, they lack a fundamental function for what Many people use to play their music: the ability to receive and make phone calls. If you are using a smartphone, these are only headphones, not headphones with a function button (like the kind that come with an iPhone, for example), and not ones that have an output through which you can speak or take dictation.
That aside, the sound quality was ok, with a somewhat tinny, canned quality and poor capability in processing deep bass or treble. If changing the levels to decrease treble, you'll see some improvement in the sound. For anything spoken word like podcasts, these are fine.
The fit is not bad. Usually, these things are big on me (female with apparently small ear-holes, if you would judge by most headphones), but these were comfortable. The three sizes of rubbery earplugs always help and are generally standard, and the ear hooks also aide in keeping them in place.

Summary:
For the price, you get decent headphones that do not have an output function.
text_fidelity_b: Philips SHQ3200BK/28 ActionFit Sports Earhook Headphones

JBL Boombox 2 - Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Powerful Sound and Monstrous Bass, IPX7 Waterproof, 24 Hours of Playtime, Powerbank, JBL PartyBoost for Speaker Pairing, for Home and Outdoor(Black) I will start this review by saying that I honestly do love this speaker But at the same time I can easily see why others might not. This is NOT the speaker that you simply grab and throw in the bag and go. This speaker is rather large and surprisingly VERY heavy.

The sound quality is nice but the bass is only ok in my opinion. I have another speaker which is made by Amazon that cost about $50 that has the exact same sound quality. It is loud but as with this bass, ive heard others that are louder and cost much less.

I will start with the app that the instructions tell you that you need to download. It states that it is for updates, but all I saw is that it is used for is linking multiple speakers together.

I wanted this speaker because we spend alot of time out by the pool and at the river during the summer. I knew that I wanted something that was water proof for both of those settings so I was happy to give this one a try. As I mentioned before, this sucker is HEAVY so while it may be water proof, if you were to drop in the river at any point it would go straight to the bottom never to be seen again, so it wouldn't really matter how water proof it is. For the pool and sitting stationary, it would be perfect.

One use that I can see us using this speaker would be for travel baseball games. It is loud enough that you would be able to hear it from a distance.

As I said earlier... some will love this speaker and think that it is absolutely worth it. Others will not. This speaker will strictly come down to personal opinion. For instance, other than the weight, I love this speaker. My spouse thinks that his $50 is much better.
text_fidelity_b: JBL Boombox 2 - Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Powerful Sound and Monstrous Bass, IPX7 Waterproof, 24 Hours of Playtime, Powerbank, JBL PartyBoost for Speaker Pairing, for Home and Outdoor(Black)

Constructed of water repellant nylon inside and out, this bag is impeccably stitched, has sturdy zippers that work flawlessly, a comfortable carry handle, and offers plenty of storage. In fact, the pack can hold two laptops up to 17" at the same time along with other gear.

Here's the layout:

Front - a 10" x 9" side opening zippered compartment, a 12" x 16" zippered compartment with 2 sleeves for cell phone, battery bank etc, 2 pen holding sleeves, plus a 10" x 4" zippered mesh compartment.

Sides - 4.5" x 7" beverage holders on each side that are large enough to accommodate even larger bottles and sit flush when not being used.

Main Compartment - double zipper provides entry and can be locked to prevent theft. Inside are two cell phone/gadget pouches, an 8" x 6" zippered compartment, and a 12" x 11" laptop or tablet sleeve with no padding on the front. I was able to fit my 15" Lenovo ThinkPad into this sleeve with room to spare and although the sleeve front isn't padded, the entire compartment t is surrounded with excellent padding. Rear - comfortable padded carry handle, the back unzips to reveal a large well padded compartment that can fit up to a 17" laptop. Directly beneath the lumbar padding is a 11" x 6" zippered compartment that would be an excellent place to secure passports, travel documents, emergency cash, or other valuables.

Straps - thickly padded, mesh lined, and ergonomically curved, with a sunglasses loop on one side. The adjustment hardware is heavy duty plastic that functions smoothly and all of the stress points are well reinforced.

This is a very well designed laptop bag made of excellent materials that should be durable. It would function well for school, business, or travel, and it seems very reasonably priced considering the quality.

text_fidelity_a: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th) I would like to give this a five rating but it is still too quirky to receive that. I deducted a star for each major problem-no control over storage and what appears to be an unstable OS. I switched from another android tablet that was giving me problems. My brother has the largest Kindle Fire HD and it looked very nice. I paid extra to get rid of the ads because they were too obtrusive. One would pop in while I was doing something and shut down that app. I wanted a device for reading e-books and listening to audio books. I also wanted something that had external storage that I could manage. Wrong. The app saves to the external storage card but the downloaded content goes directly to the device storage which makes no sense. Why have an external storage option when none of the larger content files will save to it? The sound is more treble than bass, but it sounds good. My device is only 8 GB, so it max'ed out quickly when I downloaded content. I like the thin form factor. This cuts down the amount of weight in my bag. I got the magenta with a purple cover. Maybe it is because this is the first time I am using it, but the OS is very jumpy and the screen is not as responsive as I would like. I have to tap several times to open an app or play a song. Once I figured it out, downloading from my accounts was easy. Unfortunately when I tried to view my internal content, the device went into a loop, then restarted itself and that took a long time. If I ever am able to download to my SD card as the instructions say, then I will be happy to upgrade my review. In the meantime, I am disappointed that this is not able to do what I wanted.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba Canvio Basics 1TB Portable Hard Drive - Black (HDTB310XK3AA) PERFECT!

I was looking for a MAC time machine backup drive and noticed the external drives labeled as MAC were $10 - $15 more. I then read the Q&A on this drive and someone gave the most perfect instructions:

"right out of the box it's not Mac ready, but the solution is real easy. You go to Utilities and open up Disk Utility. With the drive plugged in, select it and go to the Erase tab and there should be a drop down menu with Format. Select Mac OS and click erase and after that's done, the drive should be formatted for Mac and you can save to your heart's content."

I might only add where to find Disk Utility in case you didn't know ... in finder go to the applications folder and in that folder is utilities and in that folder is disk utility.

I did just as the person in Q&A said and the second it was done reformatting a box came up asking if I wanted to use this drive as a time machine backup drive. I said yes, and within 107 seconds I was done. Color me impressed!

We got the 1tb drive because we have a 1tb 21.5" iMac from Nov 2013.

I hope this helps someone. I will update this review later as to longevity of the drive.

UPDATE: May 6, 2018
7 months later and this little backup drive does what it should do. We have never needed to utilize the files it stores, but it is nice to know the files are there. I periodically check to make sure my Mac is recording on this drive and it functions perfectly as a time machine drive.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba Canvio Basics 1TB Portable Hard Drive - Black (HDTB310XK3AA)

text_fidelity_a:
CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact I have two of the larger Cyberpower UPS for my desktop systems and they have performed perfectly for the past (nearly) five years. So, when I needed a UPS for my cable modem and router I picked another Cyberpower. Since the draw on the two attached devices is so low I went with a lower capacity. They have other models that have about the same power output, but this model offers a screen to check load, run time, and other metrics while the unit is running. I've found that screen very helpful on my other UPS' so I went with this model.

Construction quality is very solid. There are 8 outlets - 4 for surge only (and are always on); 4 with surge and battery backup. The battery is replaceable, but I don't expect to have to do that anytime soon - both my other systems are running on their original batteries and still maintain a full charge after nearly 5 years of use.

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

I did not use the included software since I don't have a PC attached, so I can't comment on its features.

Highly recommend for a mid-level UPS system.
text_fidelity_b: CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact

I'm glad that I decided to try it for a couple of days, first. The screen is always covered with fingerprints and smudges and I find myself wiping it off many times a day. It also scratches easily. Since we're all washing our hands 40 times a day, the amount of fingerprints feels excessive to me and I hate looking at it. Even so, with the screen protector on, the screen is very responsive. Zero problems. And while I'm actually using my tablet, I don't notice the scratches or fingerprints.

There is also a shimmery rainbow effect. I don't really notice it while the screen is on and it seems to be less of an effect after the couple of weeks that I've been using it. I think because there's less of an air gap.

Everything lines up perfectly and the back part of the case also seems perfect to me. I would love to see this brand make a version that's just the well-fitted back piece.

So is it perfect? No. However, the things that bother me about it aren't really noticeable while the screen is on and I'm using it. It's protective and the screen protector doesn't interfere in the responsiveness of the screen in any way. So overall, I do think that this purchase was worth it. I'm glad that I decided to try it instead of immediately sending it back.

Another comment -- I keep a little piece of electrical tape over the front camera hole. The screen protector holds the tape in place so that I don't have to periodically change it anymore.
