text_fidelity_a:
Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive) Sony WH-XB900N Wireless Noise Canceling Extra Bass Headphones have great sound quality. Plus, for an over the ear headphone they are surprisingly lightweight. I also like how they bend to fold up and are really pliable. However, that's really where the greatness stops. Pairing these with any device I own is difficult or doesn't happen at all. These will not pair with my laptop. My laptop sees it's there. It claims it's playing from the headphones, but alas it does not most of the time. In addition, these will not play from iTunes. So, if you have an Apple device forget it. These will not pair with my iPhone 5. For two reasons, first, these are terrible with Apple devices/software and second, you must have the App to pair the headphones, which if you have an older phone won't happen because the App is only compatible with certain iOS systems. As much as I am angry with Apple for stopping all updates for older Apple devices (which work just fine otherwise), it's equally frustrating with App developers who do not design their Apps to be compatible with the older systems. So, most of my experience with these headphones is through the AUX jack.

Therefore, the sound quality is really good. I listen to a lot of hiphop and the bass is spot on. However, I do listen other types of music (pretty much everything) and I would have to say listening to Beethoven's 6th and Old Blind Dogs was a nice experience as well! The noise cancelling is a joke. I can hear everything around me still. In fact, I'm currently wearing these as I type this review and can hear the click clack of the keys, my son bump around upstairs, and my father just call my name. So, if you wear these on public transportation or at work, you're gonna hear everything as usual. But they are good headphones and comfortable on my ears.

The instructions are ridiculous. Can we stop with the picture instructions? They make no sense. I need words and should not have to depend on internet video reviews to get clarity on how to use anything. There is a way to play, pause, volume down/up by tapping or swiping, but I have no idea how to do it. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. They have a long battery life. I charged these weeks ago and they still have a charge as I use them now.

So, these have a great sound quality, the noise cancellation doesn't do anything, and you need to pair these with non-Apple devices.

I then connected the first unit to my PC through the USB port and the touchscreen began working afterward. The same cure worked on the second unit. Software glitch I thought.

By the way, the frozen unit eventually bypasses the "legal" screen (times out I suppose) and goes into the map navigation mode, although it is still unresponsive to the touch screen.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation UPDATED March 11, 2015--See Below

SHOULD YOU BUY THIS UNIT?
In my opinion, this unit, like all things Amazon, is only about 80% ready for market but they release this stuff anyway. It's a cheap shot to their customers and they should straighten up and actually release products when they have all the features advertised actually implemented.

Buy this thing only if USB isn't important to you AND if you are willing to wait hours to upload video and picture content to the Amazon Cloud Drive. ABOUT THE CLOUD DRIVE--the initial allocation of space for your account is only a few gigs (I think 2 gigs). After that you can upgrade and pay Amazon more money for the bump up in storage space. That this unit has a non-functioning, flaccid USB forces you to use their cloud for video streaming your own stuff and this works for Amazon because lots of folks will end up paying for more cloud storage. This is borderline unethical in my opinion.

Pros:
Sets up easily.
Great help videos
Outstanding picture quality
WiFi and Wired connections both very good
Small footprint

Cons:
USB not implemented so you cannot play your own video content without uploading to their cloud
Uploading to their Cloud takes much longer than other clouds (Dropbox for example). It's hours compared to minutes
Puny cloud storage allocation without upgrade
Search has no QWERTY layout to type in your search and no way to add a space and second or more words to the search
Limited on-line support

CONCLUSION: Not really ready for prime time if you need full functionality in a unit like this.

UPDATED March 11, 2015: REDUCING THIS TO TWO STARS. Okay, this is the most annoying, frustrating and unreliable piece of technology I've ever purchased. In the months since I bought this item its performance has degraded to where it is simply unacceptable. Amazon tech support is of little help and neither is Netflix tech support. Here are the NEW FEATURES my Fire TV now performs:

1) Regularly pauses an in-progress program as if I'd pressed the pause button. It usually resumes after I press the play button on the remote.
2) It does not play nice with Netflix and often (actually daily) gets hung so that I see an error message telling me there's trouble, "playing this video right now...," and suggests I try later or pick something different. Well, I don't want to wait, nor do I wish to watch something else.
3) It often cannot find my HDMI cable, even though I've tried several cables. It is, therefore, not a cable problem but an internal glitch in the Fire TV box.
4) Often after turning it on, it goes to a blank screen from which there is no return.
5) There are many more fun things this piece of garbage does but why bother list them.

Tomorrow, I'm going to Best Buy to pick up a Roku 3 for about what it sells for on Amazon. See, then I won't have to wait for it to be shipped and, if necessary, I can take it back to a real store and exchange or return it. Oh, and I intend to donate this Fire TV box to the garbage can. I do hope it won't offend the garbage man/woman/person/whatever.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only I really bought a Canon DSLR (vs Nikon, or any of the mirrorless Cameras) for this lens. I needed a low distortion very wide lens for real estate videos and I also needed image stabilization and quiet focusing. I don't think there is any other lens from any manufacturer that satisfies all of those things except this one. (Sigma has the 10-20mm but no stabilization, lower optical quality, and more money! Tamaron - 10-24 - same story. And so on ).
GOOD: Excellent optical quality for the price. This lens is noticeably sharper and has less distortion at 10mm than my kit lens 18-135mm has at 18mm. Stabilization works very well. Focusing is very fast and silent. I don't hear it even with the built in mic when shooting video (on a Canon 70D). Extremely lightweight and fairly compact.

BAD: Maximum Aperture. This is NOT a fast lens. F/4.5 maximum is not that great and you lose it pretty quickly as you zoom in since the max aperture ranges from 4.5 - 5.6. You need to have some decent light to shoot with this lens. But given the lack of competition in super wide stabilized silent EF-S lenses (or any Canon mount lens) and the price of anything vaguely similar, I think it's a reasonable compromise.

Note: At this price, you can't really call it a knock, but it'd be nice if it came with the lens hood. You can get a clone lens hood for $10 or so.

ALSO: Canon has now updated their EOS Utility software for this lens.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only

Cat8 Ethernet Cable 50FT, JEVIT Internet Network Cord, 40Gbps 2000Mhz LAN Wires, High Speed S/FTP LAN Cables with Gold Plated RJ45 Connector for Router, Modem, Gaming (15m/ 50FT） Keep in mind that since this has a PVC jacket, and since PVC produces toxic smoke, this shouldn't be run from room to room (per code) despite its long length.

Also keep in mind that cat8 doesn't do anything above cat6 unless you have a 10 or 40Gb/s NIC/SFP at both ends of your link, and the total link length is shorter than it was with cat6.

So unless you need a strong backbone link in a data center, don't think you need this.

If you are running a data center, you may want to look elsewhere: this cable appears to be hand wrapped. The connectors were pushed into the body of the roll in a way where the bend radius was dangerously close to being exceeded. I guess there's something to be said for buying the best if you're really using this for business.

Just know what you need and what you're going to do with it. For almost all home applications running from room to room, I'd take a cat6 cable with a legitimate riser or plenum rating any day.
text_fidelity_b: Cat8 Ethernet Cable 50FT, JEVIT Internet Network Cord, 40Gbps 2000Mhz LAN Wires, High Speed S/FTP LAN Cables with Gold Plated RJ45 Connector for Router, Modem, Gaming (15m/ 50FT）

The description says it does not come with an SD card or AAA batteries, but mine did, perhaps for review purposes, although the box did not look like it had been opened. Seems like it would come with that stuff, so perhaps other reviewers might clarify. There is a case and two separate pouches for the wider camera lens and the microphone.

Functionality and video quality are pretty good. I guess the only drawback is that this almost seems like a throwback now. For still pictures - on a vacation or a great hike where I want to take great pictures - I still take along a small camera instead of just my cell phone, but the truth is cell phone cameras are getting so good now that I wonder when that will no longer seem prudent. And with that said, my small camera takes such amazing (not studio quality) HD that I wonder when something like this would really seem like the best thing, especially considering they both take SD cards and length is only limited by SD card capacity.

It certainly does seem like a more professional camera in its size and shape, but mostly because that style has been the trend for some time now. But in a way this style is already starting to seem outdated, like a throwback. I also noticed, just now, that even the really big name manufacturers have this style in 1080p for comparable prices.

I'd definitely give this thing a look. I would have totally loved it a few years ago. The mic and extra lens still feel like premium features, but I'm rarely the one to set up for photos and video footage, as I usually just do landscapes or great spontaneous moments. This may be a fantastic alternative to giving kids your phone - or a phone - to play with. Seems like a good way to encourage their inner photographer without it leading into a bunch of cheap phone games.

Camera has mini* USB and HDMI ports (as opposed to micro) - just when I was wondering what I'd ever do with this one mini-HDMI cable I have... Mic takes 2xCR2032 batteries, which are included, and should probably last, as I don't think mics eat up much power. Has a curled, springy, analogue audio cable with stereo mini-plugs on both ends to connect the mic. Also has an external battery charger.
text_fidelity_b: HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder
